title: Budget Billing Terms and Conditions — Deferred Balance, Late Payment Basis and Annual Settle-Up
content:
# Budget Billing Terms and Conditions — Deferred Balance, Late Payment Basis and Annual Settle-Up

**1. Deferred balance.** While a Budget Billing plan is in effect, the difference between each regular bill's actual charges and the plan installment is carried on the plan as a deferred balance. A positive deferred balance is the amount by which actual charges have run beyond the plan installments; a negative deferred balance is the amount by which they have fallen short of the installments. The balance is carried until it is recovered, settled or closed out.

**2. Posting of the monthly deferral or recovery.** On every plan, the monthly deferral or recovery is booked on the bill date of every regular bill while the plan is active.

**3. Late payment charges.** On every plan, while the plan is active, a late payment charge is computed on the unpaid portion of the bill after the deferral or recovery entry of that bill.

**4. Annual settle-up.** The terms of the annual settle-up differ by plan:

| Plan | Deferred balance settled annually | Bill that carries the annual settle-up | Smallest absolute deferred balance settled at the annual settle-up |
|---|---|---|---|
| Residential Levelized Billing Plan | No | Not applicable | $0.00 |
| Residential Budget Billing Plan | Yes | The regular bill dated in the calendar month of the enrollment anniversary | $10.00 |
| Residential FlatBill Plan | No | Not applicable | $0.00 |
| Commercial Levelized Billing Plan | No | Not applicable | $0.00 |
| Commercial Budget Billing Plan | Yes | The regular bill dated in the calendar month of the enrollment anniversary | $25.00 |
| Small Business FlatBill Plan | No | Not applicable | $0.00 |

At an annual settle-up, a deferred balance whose absolute value is smaller than the plan's minimum is not settled and carries over.

## Clauses 3 and 4 applied (hypothetical figures)

*Late payment basis.* A bill under an active plan shows actual charges of $162.00 against an installment of $140.00; the $22.00 excess is deferred, leaving $140.00 due. If the customer pays $100.00 by the due date, the unpaid portion after the deferral entry is $40.00, and that is the amount a late payment charge is computed on.

*Annual settle-up thresholds.*

| Plan | Deferred balance on the anniversary-month bill | Settled at the annual settle-up |
|---|---|---|
| Residential Budget Billing Plan | $9.99 owed | No — below $10.00, carries over |
| Residential Budget Billing Plan | $10.00 owed | Yes — the $10.00 is billed |
| Residential Budget Billing Plan | $42.50 in the customer's favour | Yes — the $42.50 is credited |
| Commercial Budget Billing Plan | $24.00 in the customer's favour | No — below $25.00, carries over |
| Commercial Budget Billing Plan | $25.00 owed | Yes — the $25.00 is billed |

*Anniversary month.* For a hypothetical Residential Budget Billing Plan enrolled on 14 March, the annual settle-up is carried by the regular bill dated in March of each following year, whatever the day of March on which that bill is dated.
